title: Read one partition
summary: A Cassandra query is efficient when it names the partition key.
introduction: A Cassandra query is efficient when it names the partition key. Your task: Read a different sample reader id.
learningObjectives: Read a different sample reader id.
Explain the example for read one partition

blocks.text: A Cassandra query is efficient when it names the partition key. It can then read the rows grouped under that key.
Use a local single-node Cassandra 4+ practice cluster and cqlsh. The SimpleStrategy keyspace below is only for that local lesson. These commands do not run in this site's SQLite playground.

blocks.code: SELECT day,title,pages FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='mia';
blocks.title: Read one partition

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.
`WHERE` keeps only rows that pass its condition. Check the condition with sample data before using it for a change.

blocks.text: The query returns Mia's stored days in the table's clustering order.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not expect arbitrary joins and filters to work like PostgreSQL. Model tables for the reads you need.
